literal: At the burial, from princes and dukes downward all escorted him beyond the suburbs.
idiomatic: At the burial, princes and dukes alike escorted him beyond the city.

literal: He received paired sacrifice in the temple hall of Emperor Wen.
idiomatic: He was given paired sacrifice in Emperor Wen's temple.

literal: Jin had stratagems and was skilled at serving superiors.
idiomatic: Jin was resourceful and skilled at serving his superiors.

literal: Though his fame and rank were weighty, he became all the more humble; each time he went to court he took no more than two or three mounted followers.
idiomatic: For all his rank he grew more modest; going to court he took only two or three riders.

literal: Whenever the court had military or state affairs, it mostly decided them with Jin.
idiomatic: Whenever the court faced army or state matters, it mostly settled them with Jin.

literal: Jin also exhausted his wisdom; therefore among the meritorious he was especially entrusted, from beginning to end as one, and no man spoke against him.
idiomatic: Jin gave his wit fully; among the great ministers he alone was trusted start to finish, without a whisper against him.

literal: He always admonished his sons to keep to quiet withdrawal.
idiomatic: He always warned his sons to seek quiet and withdrawal.

literal: Moreover his years were very long and his honors heavy; his sons and grandsons multiplied, all reaching high eminence—none in the time compared.
idiomatic: He lived to great age in heavy honor; his descendants multiplied and rose high—none could match it then.

literal: His son Shi succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Shi succeeded him.

literal: Shi, styled Bingshi, was from youth gentle and generous; for military merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wannian.
idiomatic: Shi, styled Bingshi, was gentle from youth; for military merit he was made Viscount of Wannian.

literal: In the fourteenth year of Datong he was promoted in succession to Master of Writing.
idiomatic: In Datong year fourteen he rose to Master of Writing.

literal: That year Zhou Emperor Wen and the Wei heir apparent toured west; Shi then followed on the journey.
idiomatic: That year Yuwen Tai and the Wei crown prince toured west; Shi went with them.

literal: Yuwen Tai carved stone on Long Mountain, recording the meritorious by name and rank in order and carving them; Shi was beforehand named Opening the Government with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and only in the fifteenth year was the appointment conferred.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai carved the meritorious on Long Mountain in order of rank; Shi was named in advance to Opening the Government with Three Excellencies' standing, but received it only in year fifteen.

literal: Shortly he was made Governor of Wei Prefecture, specially granted one set of drums and pipes, and advanced in rank to duke.
idiomatic: Soon he was Governor of Wei, granted drums and pipes, and raised to duke.

literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, the Qiang chieftain Donglingjie led his tribes in revolt, linking west with Tuyuhun.
idiomatic: In Emperor Gong's second year the Qiang chieftain Donglingjie rebelled, allying west with Tuyuhun.

literal: The great general Doulu Ning campaigned against him but for a long time could not overcome him.
idiomatic: The great general Doulu Ning campaigned but could not break him.

literal: Shi was again sent; he then defeated them.
idiomatic: Shi was sent again and defeated them.

literal: Yuwen Tai wrote in his own hand to comfort and inquire, granting a hundred male and female slaves and a hundred horses.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai wrote in his own hand to praise him, granting a hundred slaves and a hundred horses.

literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was appointed Chief of the Households Bureau and advanced in fief to Duke of Yanshou.
idiomatic: When Xiaomin took the throne, he became Chief of the Households Bureau and Duke of Yanshou.

literal: In the second year of Tianhe, the Pu River bandits of Yan Province, the outlaw Hao Sanlang, rebelled and attacked Dan Province.
idiomatic: In Tianhe year two, Hao Sanlang of Yan's Pu River rebelled and attacked Dan.

literal: Shi was sent to pacify them and was then made Governor of Yan.
idiomatic: Shi was sent to crush them and was made Governor of Yan.

literal: In the fifth year he inherited the ducal title of Yan and was advanced to Pillar of State.
idiomatic: In year five he inherited the dukedom of Yan and became Pillar of State.

literal: He was dismissed for a crime.
idiomatic: He was dismissed for a crime.

literal: Shortly his former office was restored and he was made Commander-in-Chief of Liang.
idiomatic: Soon his office was restored and he was made Commander-in-Chief of Liang.

literal: In the second year of Daxiang he was further made Supreme Pillar of State and appointed Grand Left Assistant.
idiomatic: In Daxiang year two he was made Supreme Pillar of State and Grand Left Assistant.

literal: In the first year of Sui's founding he died; posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous title An.
idiomatic: In Sui's founding year he died, posthumously Minister of Works, titled An.

literal: His son Yan.
idiomatic: His son Yan.

literal: Yan, styled Yuanwu, was eight feet tall with fine beard and brows.
idiomatic: Yan, styled Yuanwu, stood eight feet with handsome beard and brows.

literal: Zhou's Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu saw him and valued him, giving him his daughter in marriage.
idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, Zhou's Grand Chancellor, favored him and gave him his daughter.

literal: Because of his father's merit he was granted the fief of Duke of Xinye.
idiomatic: For his father's merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Xinye.

literal: He served in succession as Left and Right Palace Defender and Governor of Ying.
idiomatic: He served as Left and Right Palace Defender and Governor of Ying in turn.

literal: In the Daxiang era, as Commander of the Water Army he followed Wei Xiaokuan in planning for Huainan.
idiomatic: Under Daxiang he commanded the water army under Wei Xiaokuan in Huainan.

literal: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, the commander Zhao Wenbiao and Yan had long been at odds; Yan intended to deal with him and therefore lay in his pavilion feigning illness.
idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Commander Zhao Wenbiao was Yan's enemy; Yan feigned illness in his pavilion to trap him.

literal: Wenbiao came alone; Yan killed him.
idiomatic: Wenbiao came alone; Yan killed him.

literal: He then said Wenbiao had conspired with Jiong; his subordinates dared not move.
idiomatic: He claimed Wenbiao had conspired with Jiong; his troops dared not stir.

literal: At the time Emperor Wen of Sui, because Jiong was not yet pacified, feared Yan would again raise border trouble and therefore pardoned and released him, at once appointing him Commander of Wu.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen, Jiong not yet down, feared Yan would stir the frontier and pardoned him, making him Commander of Wu at once.

literal: For repeatedly defeating Chen armies he was granted several hundred bolts of colored silk.
idiomatic: For repeated victories over Chen he was granted hundreds of bolts of silk.

literal: When Sui received the abdication, Wenbiao's younger brother came to court saying his brother was innocent.
idiomatic: When Sui took the throne, Wenbiao's brother came to court pleading his innocence.

literal: The emperor ordered the matter investigated; the Grand Tutor Dou Chi and others judged Yan should die.
idiomatic: The emperor ordered an inquiry; Grand Tutor Dou Chi and others ruled Yan should die.

literal: The emperor, because his house had outstanding merit, especially pardoned him and demoted him to Opening the Government.
idiomatic: The emperor, honoring the family's merit, pardoned him specially and demoted him to Opening the Government.

literal: Later he inherited the title Duke of Yan.
idiomatic: Later he inherited the dukedom of Yan.

literal: Shortly he was appointed Governor of Ze.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Governor of Ze.

literal: Dismissed, he died at home.
idiomatic: Dismissed, he died at home.

literal: His son Shiqian.
idiomatic: His son Shiqian.

literal: Yan's younger brother Zhongwen.
idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Zhongwen.

literal: Zhongwen, styled Ciwu, was from youth clever and keen; while still in childhood he went to study and was absorbed in learning without tiring.
idiomatic: Zhongwen, styled Ciwu, was clever as a boy; he studied without tiring even in childhood.

literal: His father Shi marveled at him and said: "This boy will surely raise our clan."
idiomatic: His father Shi said in wonder, "This boy will raise our house."

literal: At nine he once met Zhou Emperor Wen at Yunyang Palace.
idiomatic: At nine he met Yuwen Tai at Yunyang Palace.

literal: He asked: "I hear the boy loves reading—what business has reading?"
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai asked, "I hear you love books—what is reading for?"

literal: He replied: "To support one's father and serve one's lord—loyalty and filial piety, that is all."
idiomatic: He answered, "To support one's father and serve one's lord—loyalty and filial piety, nothing more."

literal: Yuwen Tai greatly sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai sighed in deep admiration.

literal: Later he studied under the Erudite Li Xiang and received the Book of Changes and the Three Rites, grasping the great principles in outline.
idiomatic: Later he studied the Changes and the Three Rites under Erudite Li Xiang and grasped their main points.

literal: When grown he was free and easy with great ambition, his spirit and tone outstanding.
idiomatic: Grown, he was bold and ambitious, his bearing striking.

literal: He began his career as Attendant to the Prince of Zhao and Governor of Angu.
idiomatic: He began as Attendant to the Prince of Zhao and Governor of Angu.

literal: The Ren and Du families each lost an ox; later one ox was found and both families claimed it; the prefecture and district long could not decide.
idiomatic: The Ren and Du families each lost an ox; when one was found both claimed it, and the prefecture could not decide.

literal: Han Bojun, chief clerk of Yi Province, said: "The youth of Angu is clever and perceptive—he can be ordered to decide it."
idiomatic: Yi Province chief clerk Han Bojun said, "The young man of Angu is sharp—let him decide."

literal: Zhongwen said: "This is easy to resolve."
idiomatic: Zhongwen said, "That is easily settled."

literal: He then ordered the two families each to drive their herds of oxen forward and released the disputed ox; the ox at once went toward the Ren family's herd.
idiomatic: He had both herds driven up and turned the disputed ox loose; it walked straight to Ren's herd.

literal: He also had men slightly wound the ox; the Ren family lamented, the Du family were at ease.
idiomatic: He had the ox lightly hurt; Ren's people wailed, Du's were unmoved.

literal: Zhongwen then sternly questioned the Du family; they confessed guilt and left.
idiomatic: Zhongwen pressed the Du family; they confessed and withdrew.

literal: Qu Tu Shang, Governor of Shizhou, was a partisan of Yuwen Hu.
idiomatic: Qu Tu Shang of Shizhou was Yuwen Hu's man.

literal: He had earlier been imprisoned for an offense; none dared prosecute him.
idiomatic: He had been jailed for a crime; none dared touch him.

literal: When Zhongwen reached the commandery he investigated to the end and completed the case.
idiomatic: When Zhongwen took the commandery he investigated to the end and closed the case.

literal: In Shu they said: "For clear judgment without peer there is Duke Yu; for not shunning the powerful there is Ciwu."
idiomatic: Shu said, "Clear judgment without peer—Duke Yu; fearing no power—Ciwu."

literal: He was summoned as Junior Master of Rectitude, enfeoffed Duke of Yanshou, and for merit granted ceremonial rank equal to Opening the Government.
idiomatic: He was summoned as Junior Master of Rectitude, made Duke of Yanshou, and for merit given Opening the Government's ceremonial rank.

literal: Under Emperor Xuan he was Governor of Dong Commandery.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he was Governor of Dong Commandery.

literal: When Yuchi Jiong raised rebellion he sent to entice Zhongwen; Zhongwen refused him.
idiomatic: When Jiong rebelled he tried to win Zhongwen; Zhongwen refused.

literal: Jiong sent the ceremonial peer Yuwen Wei to attack him.
idiomatic: Jiong sent Yuwen Wei to attack him.

literal: Zhongwen met the attack and greatly defeated Wei; for the merit he was appointed Opening the Government.
idiomatic: Zhongwen met him and routed him; for the merit he was made Opening the Government.

literal: Jiong again sent his general Yuwen Zhou to cross the Stone Ford.
idiomatic: Jiong again sent Yuwen Zhou across the Stone Ford.

literal: Yuwen Wei and Zou Shao from Baima—the two routes advanced together and again attacked Zhongwen.
idiomatic: Yuwen Wei and Zou Shao came from Baima; two columns struck again.

literal: The commandery men Helian Sengqie and Jing Zizhe led the masses to respond to Jiong.
idiomatic: Helian Sengqie and Jing Zizhe of the commandery rallied men to Jiong.

literal: Zhongwen judged himself unable to hold; he abandoned wife and children, broke the encirclement and fled, reaching the capital.
idiomatic: Seeing he could not hold, he left wife and children, broke out, and reached the capital.

literal: Jiong slaughtered his three sons and one daughter.
idiomatic: Jiong killed his three sons and one daughter.

literal: Emperor Wen of Sui led him into the inner chamber and wept for him, granting five hundred bolts of colored silk and two hundred taels of gold.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen brought him to the inner chamber and wept, granting five hundred bolts of silk and two hundred taels of gold.

literal: He was advanced to Great General and made Commander-in-Chief on the Henan Circuit, granted drums and pipes.
idiomatic: He was made Great General and Commander-in-Chief on the Henan circuit, with drums and pipes.

literal: He rode post-horses to Luoyang to raise troops and campaign against Jiong's general Tan Rang.
idiomatic: He raced to Luoyang to raise troops against Jiong's general Tan Rang.

literal: At the time Wei Xiaokuan held Jiong at Yong Bridge.
idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan then held Jiong at Yong Bridge.

literal: Zhongwen went to him and they deliberated plans.
idiomatic: Zhongwen went to him to plan.

literal: The commander Yuwen Xin was rather suspicious on his own account and therefore said to Zhongwen: "Yuchi Jiong is truly not hard to pacify; I only fear that after matters settle there will again be the worry of 'the bow hidden when the birds are gone.'"
idiomatic: Commander Yuwen Xin was suspicious and said to Zhongwen, "Jiong is easy—but when birds are gone, bows are stored away. I fear that after victory."

literal: Zhongwen feared Xin would change; he said to him: "The Chancellor is generous and magnanimous, clear-sighted and ample; in three days in the capital I frequently saw three goods—he is no ordinary man."
idiomatic: Fearing Xin would turn, Zhongwen said, "The Chancellor is generous and far-sighted; in three days in the capital I saw three virtues—no ordinary man."

literal: Xin said: "What are the three goods like?"
idiomatic: Xin asked, "What three?"

literal: Zhongwen said: "There was Chen Wandi newly come from the rebels; the Chancellor at once had his younger brother Nandi recruit village men to follow the army in suppressing bandits."
idiomatic: Zhongwen said, "Chen Wandi had just defected; the Chancellor had his brother Nandi raise village men to fight bandits."

literal: That is the first magnanimity.
idiomatic: That is magnanimity—the first.

literal: Superior Gentleman Song Qian was sent on a mission to investigate; Qian used this to seek other crimes on the side.
idiomatic: Song Qian was sent to investigate; he used it to hunt other crimes.

literal: The Chancellor reproved him saying: 'Those caught in the net can be pursued within it—why must you inquire separately and harm the great principle.'
idiomatic: The Chancellor rebuked him: 'Those in the net can be pursued—why hunt elsewhere and harm the whole?'

literal: That is the second—not seeking private advantage from men.
idiomatic: That is the second—not fishing for private gain.

literal: When he spoke of Zhongwen's wife and children he never failed to shed tears.
idiomatic: Speaking of Zhongwen's wife and children he never failed to weep.

literal: That is the third—having a benevolent heart.
idiomatic: That is the third—a benevolent heart.

literal: Xin from this was then at ease.
idiomatic: Xin was reassured.

literal: Zhongwen's army reached east of Bian Province and repeatedly defeated Jiong's generals.
idiomatic: Zhongwen's army reached east of Bian and repeatedly beat Jiong's generals.

literal: He attacked Liang Commandery; Jiong's defending general Liu Xiaokuan abandoned the city and fled.
idiomatic: He attacked Liang; Liu Xiaokuan abandoned the city and fled.

literal: At first, at Liaodi, the generals all said: "The army has come from afar, weary and spent—it cannot give battle."
idiomatic: At Liaodi the generals said, "We are far from home and spent—we cannot fight."

literal: Zhongwen ordered them to take food quickly and form ranks; before long they defeated the bandits.
idiomatic: Zhongwen ordered a quick meal and battle lines; soon the enemy was broken.

literal: The generals asked the reason; he smiled and said: "The officers and men under my command are all men of Shandong, bold in swift advance—not fit for a long stand."
idiomatic: Asked why, he smiled, "My men are Shandongers—swift attack, not a long fight."

literal: "Striking them while the momentum held—that is why we won."
idiomatic: "Strike while hot—that is how we win."

literal: The generals all said: "Not what we could reach."
idiomatic: The generals said, "Beyond us."

literal: He pressed the attack on Cao Province, capturing Jiong's appointed Governor Li Zhongkang and the ceremonial peer Fang Jin.
idiomatic: He pressed Cao, taking Jiong's governor Li Zhongkang and the ceremonial peer Fang Jin.

literal: Tan Rang with the remaining troops camped at Chengwu, thinking Zhongwen could not arrive suddenly, and was just beating oxen to feast the officers.
idiomatic: Tan Rang camped at Chengwu with the remnant, sure Zhongwen could not come at once, feasting his men.

literal: Zhongwen chose cavalry to strike him and then took Chengwu.
idiomatic: Zhongwen chose cavalry, struck, and took Chengwu.
